selected.rationale: Loss on the Basket.API->RabbitMQ edge drops the checkout integration event before it is persisted; Basket.API has no durable outbox, so orders are never created and no recovery is triggered.
A delay on WebApp->Basket.API makes cart and checkout requests hang; without timeout or circuit-breaker protection, latency propagates into the UI and consumes web-server resources.
Packet loss between Basket.API and Redis removes access to the cart state, causing add/load/checkout operations to fail; Basket.API lacks a fallback, turning a transient loss into availability loss.
Injected delay on WebApp->Ordering.API stalls order-history/status calls and propagates latency to end users, exposing missing timeout or retry defenses on a synchronous user-facing path.
A BFF-to-Catalog.API delay badly degrades mobile product browsing; the BFF lacks explicit deadlines, so the mobile app waits for the full injected latency.
Delayed WebApp->Catalog.API calls block product catalog rendering; with no bounded client timeout, the storefront remains unacceptably slow under latency faults.
Loss on the mobile BFF->Ordering.API edge prevents order submission or tracking from mobile clients; no retry/recovery is available, resulting in immediate user-facing failure.
A delay in WebApp->Identity.API hangs the login/authentication flow; the edge has no visible timeout, so all web users can be blocked during the injected delay.
